hero_text: Young people giving, going and serving so the Gospel can move farther. In 2026, we are rallying AOG youth across Guyana around a practical missions goal: helping complete roofs for three missionary churches.
about_text:
Speed the Light (STL) is the youth missions initiative of the Assemblies of God that empowers young people to help advance the Gospel through missions giving.

Through Speed the Light, young people raise funds to provide missionaries with essential resources such as vehicles, transportation, communication equipment, media tools, and other ministry resources that help them reach communities and share the message of Jesus Christ more effectively. Assemblies of God
Speed the Light began in the 1940s with a simple vision: give young people a practical way to participate in the Great Commission. What started with raising funds for missionary transportation has grown into a worldwide missions effort supporting ministry in many different ways. AG News

For National Youth Ministries Guyana, Speed the Light is more than fundraising. It is about developing a generation of young people who understand missions, generosity, sacrifice, and responsibility for taking the Gospel beyond their own church and community.
project_title: Three missionary churches. One united goal.
project_text: Our 2026 target is to raise funds to help complete roofs and other essential building needs for three missionary churches.
event_text: Churches can shape Speed the Light Day in a way that fits their local ministry: a youth-led service, missions emphasis, fundraiser, outreach or hands-on service project.
director_bio:
Rev. Dr. Winston Assanah is a pastor, educator, mentor, and national youth leader who has dedicated more than three decades to Christian ministry and the development of young people. He serves as the National Youth Ministries Director of the Assemblies of God in Guyana, a position he has held since 2010, providing leadership to youth ministries across Guyana and helping to develop the next generation of Christian leaders. First Assembly Wortmanville.

His ministry is driven by a passion to see young people discover their God-given purpose, grow in their relationship with Jesus Christ, and become equipped to serve their churches, communities, and nation. Through National Youth Ministries, he has helped coordinate youth conferences, leadership development initiatives, evangelistic programmes, and other national activities designed to engage and empower young people. First Assembly Wortmanville

Rev. Dr. Assanah also serves as Senior Assistant Pastor of First Assembly of God Wortmanville, Georgetown. His academic background includes studies in theology, business management, education, and transformational leadership, including a Master of Arts in Transformational Leadership from Bakke University, a Bachelor’s degree in Theology from the Caribbean School of Theology, and a Bachelor of Science in Business Management from the University of Guyana. First Assembly Wortmanville.

As National Youth Ministries continues to advance initiatives such as Speed the Light, Rev. Dr. Assanah remains committed to mobilising young people not only to participate in ministry, but also to actively support missions and the advancement of the Gospel.
giving_text: You may also give through your local YM President , Youth Pastor or Sectional Representative or drop off funds at the Assemblies of God Head Office, Lance & Gibbs Street, Queenstown, Georgetown, Guyana.
